result.summary: Lantern Services has sent a £75.11 invoice, but nothing on file shows the engineer visited or fixed the washing machine. The day before, the contractor (Harper) phoned asking for a callback to schedule his visit. I haven't passed the invoice on. Instead I asked the contractor for a job report and an itemised invoice copy, and asked the tenant whether the visit happened and the machine now heats. The case is on hold with a 3-day follow-up.

judgement.why_this_decision: The landlord approved the engineer visit with no cost limit (event 008, approval 39). An invoice is now in (event 024), but there's no report of the visit or the outcome. Event 022 (27/02) suggests the visit hadn't happened yet: Harper asked for a callback to schedule it. The visit dates on file also disagree (event 016 says Tuesday 1pm, events 017–019 say 23/02 at 3:25pm). Paying for unconfirmed work would break the rule against acting on invoices that don't match the job. The contractor and tenant can both clear this up, so I asked them rather than escalating.

alternatives_considered.option: Forward the invoice to the landlord or pass it for payment
alternatives_considered.why_not: Nothing confirms the work was done, event 022 suggests no visit yet, and the invoice document isn't visible.
The contractor and tenant can answer this directly. Escalate if they don't reply or the answers don't match.

alternatives_considered.option: Do nothing and keep waiting on the invoice hold
alternatives_considered.why_not: The invoice has arrived but can't be checked. Without these questions the job would stall.
